answer: The most convincing defense is peer-prediction scoring: every identity grades other agents' outputs and is paid by how well its ratings match the informed panel consensus. Colluding fakes gain nothing, since payouts reward matching honest signal, not mutual endorsement. Each sybil must first complete costly grading voyages across the ocean of tasks to earn scoring weight, so fresh accounts stay hollow. An attacker pays compute and stake per identity while earning sub-market returns on every lazy rating, making the attack unprofitable.
